commit.message:
Validate retained path state against local costmap (#6311)

Rebuild the #6235 retained-prune-state behavior on current main and treat an
identical reissued path as a resume candidate only. On the next
findPlanSegment() call, validate that candidate against the local costmap:
resume when it is still inside, otherwise restore the unpruned path and
continue with the normal bounded search. Preserve the #6318 end-of-path
guard and keep ControllerServer reset semantics for cancel/success versus
failure retries.

Signed-off-by: Jeremy <peace@trippyogi.com>

commit.message:
opennav_following: remove unused robot pose lookup in approachObject() (#6367)

The comment says "If the object is behind the robot, we reverse the
control", but nothing reverses anything: computeVelocityCommand() is
called with backward hardcoded to false, and robot_pose is never read
after being filled in.

It does not work as an implicit TF validation either. target_pose was
just transformed into base_frame on the lines above, so this resolves to
a base_frame -> base_frame lookup, i.e. identity -- it would yield a zero
pose even if something did read it, and it succeeds regardless of the
state of the rest of the TF tree.

Removing the block only; whether the reversing behaviour the comment
describes should actually be implemented is left as a separate question.

Signed-off-by: marcos daniel santana <Marcos.Daniel1990@hotmail.com>

commit.message:
Fix rotateToObject() using stale/empty state for its first TF lookup (#6359)

Two related bugs in opennav_following's search-by-rotating recovery path,
found while porting/testing this package on Jazzy (real robot + Gazebo):

- object_pose.header.frame_id is still empty on the very first lost-detection
  event (no detection has ever arrived yet), so the initial getCurrentPose()
  lookup always failed and aborted the goal instead of rotating to search.
  Fall back to params_->fixed_frame when empty.

- getRefinedPose()/getTrackingPose() blocks internally for up to
  detection_timeout waiting for a detection, without touching
  iteration_start_time_. By the time control reaches rotateToObject() right
  after that wait times out, iteration_start_time_ can be tens of seconds
  stale, making the first TF lookup ask for a time already evicted from the
  tf2 buffer cache ("extrapolation into the past"). Refresh it before using
  it.

Both fixes already validated on a Jazzy backport of this same code
(marcospontoexe/opennav_following@0b394d2) and on a real robot + Gazebo.

Signed-off-by: marcos daniel santana <Marcos.Daniel1990@hotmail.com>
